qc.title: USFans QC Photos: What to Check Before Shipping
qc.intro: QC photos help you review the item that reached the warehouse. Keep them separate from seller photos, and connect every image to the exact order and option.

sections.heading: Seller photos and QC answer different questions
paragraphs: A seller gallery shows how an item is presented for sale. Warehouse inspection photos show an item after it arrives. A similar-looking product or historical image is not proof of the condition of your own order.
Product pages in this directory identify the seller gallery separately. When verified QC data is missing, the page says so rather than labeling listing photos as an inspection.

sections.heading: A practical inspection sequence
paragraphs: Start with the product, color and size you ordered. Look at the overall shape before zooming into seams, closures, printing and visible damage. For fit, compare useful measurements with a garment you already own.

If an important detail is not visible, ask USFans whether an additional photo or measurement is available and review any charge before requesting it. A photograph cannot establish every material property, internal function or long-term durability.

sections.heading: Resolve uncertainty before parcel submission
paragraphs: Keep the order number, selected option and relevant photo together when contacting support. Describe the specific mismatch instead of only saying that the item looks wrong.

USFans provides inspection and after-sales information in its Help Center. Seller return conditions and the item’s current status affect the available next step; do not assume every issue can be resolved after international shipment.

guide.title: How to Buy on USFans: Your First Order Guide
guide.intro: Finding an item, purchasing it and shipping a parcel are separate decisions. Use the official workflow and check the details at each handoff.

sections.heading: 1. Start from the correct listing
paragraphs: Browse the spreadsheet or use a product keyword. Open a listing to review its available photos and marketplace item ID. The purchase button takes that item to USFans with the appropriate marketplace code.
Use the live USFans page to confirm the selected option, price and seller information. A directory price is a reference, not an order quotation.

sections.heading: 2. Register and review the item order
paragraphs: Create your account on the USFans registration page. Account details, payment information and order management stay with USFans; this directory does not collect them.

Select the precise color, size and quantity. Review the item amount and any domestic delivery charge before submitting the order. If a link or option does not load correctly, resolve it before payment.

sections.heading: 3. Inspect the warehouse result
paragraphs: After the seller dispatches the item and it reaches the warehouse, review the order’s inspection information and photos. Confirm that the item and option match your order.
For uncertain dimensions or a visible mismatch, use the available support process before submitting the parcel. Keep written notes and relevant photos tied to the order number.

sections.heading: 4. Choose the parcel and route
paragraphs: Select the stored items you want to send, confirm your destination details and compare the routes actually available for those goods. Weight, packed dimensions, item restrictions and packaging choices can affect the options.
Review the shipping payment and any selected services in your account. After dispatch, follow the parcel’s tracking information; an estimate is not a guaranteed arrival date.

shipping.title: USFans Shipping: Costs, Routes & Tracking
shipping.intro: An item’s listed price is only one part of the total. Review domestic delivery, parcel weight, packed dimensions and the actual route quote before committing to international shipping.

sections.heading: Item cost and shipping are separate
paragraphs: The directory displays an estimated USD item price derived from the source listing. It does not include a guaranteed international shipping quote. Seller prices, selected variants and exchange rates can change.

USFans’ beginner guide describes item purchasing and international parcel submission as separate stages. Review the amounts shown at each stage instead of treating the first payment as the final delivered cost.

sections.heading: Use actual weight and packed dimensions
paragraphs: A light but bulky parcel can be priced differently from a compact parcel of the same weight. Routes may use actual weight, volumetric weight or other billing rules. Apply the rule shown for the route you are considering.
The official guide explains that shipping deposits use estimates and that final charges depend on the carrier’s checked weight and dimensions. Keep any estimate and the eventual parcel bill distinct.

sections.heading: Choose packaging with the item in mind
paragraphs: Compare available removal, protection and reinforcement options against the goods you are sending. Removing bulky packaging may reduce volume, but packaging also protects shape and surfaces.

Consolidation can simplify parcel planning, but more items in one box does not automatically produce the lowest total. Different product restrictions, route limits and delivery priorities may favor different groupings.

sections.heading: Check the live route information
paragraphs: Use the routes and services offered for your actual destination and goods. Review the quoted cost, tracking service and stated estimate together; there is no single shipping time or per-kilogram price for every order.

If a tracking event is unclear, compare the USFans parcel record with the carrier information and contact support with the parcel number. Avoid treating a temporary lack of scans as proof that the parcel is lost.

faq.q: What does USFans do?
faq.a: USFans acts as a shopping agent: it purchases requested goods from sellers, receives them at its warehouse, and helps arrange onward shipping. Your seller, warehouse processing and international carrier are separate parts of the journey.
faq.sourceTitle: What Is the Shopping Agent Service?

faq.q: How do I register with USFans?
faq.a: Use the official registration page and enter your email address, username and password. Keep access to that email so you can receive account and order messages. Registration and account details are handled by USFans.
faq.sourceTitle: Registering with USFans

faq.q: How can I find an item on USFans?
faq.a: The official beginner guide describes pasting a product link, searching by product name, or uploading a product image. On this independent site, catalog searches use the connected product source; the final order is placed on USFans.
faq.sourceTitle: Beginner’s Guide

faq.q: Why are there two payment stages?
faq.a: The first payment covers the item and delivery within China. After warehouse arrival, you select items and a shipping route, then pay the international shipping amount. Estimate the whole journey before placing the item order.
faq.sourceTitle: Three Things You Need to Know Before Using the Shopping Agent Service for the First Time

faq.q: What should I include in my USFans budget?
faq.a: Allow for the product, seller-to-warehouse delivery, international shipping, applicable customs charges and any optional services you select. A product-card price alone is not the delivered total. Review the amounts shown for your actual order.
faq.sourceTitle: How Does the Shopping Agent Service Charge?

faq.q: Do I need Chinese yuan to pay?
faq.a: USFans supports payments in other currencies through its available payment methods. Check the displayed conversion, payment-provider charges and total before confirming a payment; the amount shown for your transaction is the relevant figure.
faq.sourceTitle: Can I Pay If I Don't Have Chinese Yuan?

faq.q: Which payment methods does USFans list?
faq.a: The official help page lists PayPal, credit cards, Google Pay and account balance. Use the methods actually offered in your checkout, since the available choices for a particular transaction may differ.
faq.sourceTitle: Available Payment Methods

faq.q: Why can an item become unavailable after I order?
faq.a: A seller’s listing may not reflect current stock. USFans says availability is ultimately confirmed with the seller during purchasing. A listing or spreadsheet entry does not reserve the product for you.
faq.sourceTitle: The Online Platform Shows "In Stock" — Why Does USFans Say "Out of Stock"?

faq.q: Can I change an order after submitting it?
faq.a: Contact the purchasing agent promptly. Before seller dispatch, USFans may negotiate a change. Once the seller has shipped, changing the item may require an eligible return after warehouse arrival and a new order; return shipping can apply.
faq.sourceTitle: Can I Modify My Order After It Has Been Submitted?

faq.q: Why does a paid order show an outstanding balance?
faq.a: The official help page says seller price changes or Chinese domestic delivery charges can create a balance after submission. Read the explanation on the order page and resolve the amount requested there.
faq.sourceTitle: My Shopping Agent Order Has Been Paid — Why Do I Need to Pay an Outstanding Balance?

faq.q: What does “Pending for Confirmation” mean?
faq.a: USFans needs you to confirm some information about the item. Open the order page, read the specific question and reply there so the agent can continue processing the order.
faq.sourceTitle: What Does "Pending for Confirmation" Mean?

faq.q: Why is an item “Received” but missing from My Warehouse?
faq.a: Received indicates arrival at the warehouse. Weighing and inspection still take place before the item becomes Stored. Once that processing is complete, it appears on the Warehouse page for parcel submission.
faq.sourceTitle: My Order Shows "Received" — Why Can't I See My Items in My Warehouse?

faq.q: What should I do when an item becomes “Stored”?
faq.a: Open the Warehouse page, review the item information and photos, then select the items you want to submit for delivery. Check the address, available route, packaging choices and payable amount before confirming the parcel.
faq.sourceTitle: What Should I Do After My Items' Status Shows "Stored"?

faq.q: What does USFans check when an item arrives?
faq.a: Its help pages describe a basic visual inspection for issues such as the ordered color or label size and obvious damage. Review the resulting photos yourself and raise visible problems promptly; inspection is not a guarantee of every product detail.
faq.sourceTitle: Do You Help Me with Quality Checks?

faq.q: Does QC guarantee that clothing will fit?
faq.a: No. The detailed inspection scope refers to the size on the label or tag and states that actual size differences are outside its standard checks. Compare seller measurements with a garment you own and request relevant measurements if needed.
faq.sourceTitle: Inspection Scopes of USFans Shopping Agent Service

faq.q: Are electronics powered on during warehouse QC?
faq.a: USFans’ detailed inspection scope says electronic and digital products receive an appearance check, not a power-on test. A sealed box may also limit what can be checked inside. Do not treat an arrival photo as a functional test.
faq.sourceTitle: Inspection Scopes of USFans Shopping Agent Service

faq.q: Can I request close-up or measurement photos?
faq.a: Ask whether additional close-up or measurement photos are available for your order and confirm any charge first. Specify the item, view and measurement endpoints. If a standard image is unclear, request clarification rather than assuming it proves the item’s condition.
faq.sourceTitle: USFans Detailed Photo

faq.q: How long can goods remain in the USFans warehouse?
faq.a: The official beginner guide advertises 90 days of free storage. Check the deadline and applicable service conditions for each item in your account; do not assume forwarding orders use the same period. Ask support about unclear dates or extension terms before the deadline.
faq.sourceTitle: USFans beginner guide

faq.q: Can purchases made at different times go in one parcel?
faq.a: USFans says stored items may be selected for combined delivery or sent in separate batches. First check that their mailing restrictions and packaging requirements are compatible, and that none is approaching its storage deadline.
faq.sourceTitle: Will products purchased at different times be shipped together or in separate batches?

faq.q: Does combining items always reduce shipping cost?
faq.a: Consolidation can reduce repeated first-weight or per-parcel charges. It is still worth comparing the eligible parcel options: final dimensions, chargeable weight and route restrictions affect the total, so do not assume every larger parcel is cheaper.
faq.sourceTitle: Why should I combine delivery?

faq.q: Why can some warehouse items not be shipped together?
faq.a: Mailing restrictions may prevent a shared route, and an item marked for separate packaging cannot be submitted with other products. Review the individual restrictions instead of assuming every warehouse item can be combined.
faq.sourceTitle: Why can't the stored goods be submitted together for delivery?

faq.q: What if no shipping route is available?
faq.a: Check the unavailable-route explanation shown in your account. Confirm the actual destination, item restrictions, weight and packed dimensions. Ask support which restriction applies; do not change the destination or misstate the goods to force a route to appear.
faq.sourceTitle: What if there are no routes to choose from when submitting a parcel for delivery?

faq.q: What is the difference between actual and volumetric weight?
faq.a: Actual weight includes the goods and packaging. Volumetric weight reflects parcel size. Some routes charge using the greater figure, and the divisor varies by carrier or route; apply the rule displayed for the route you are choosing.
faq.sourceTitle: Actual Weight and Volumetric Weight

faq.q: Why can final shipping differ from the initial estimate?
faq.a: The estimate is made before final packing. Warehouse measurements, packaging changes or the carrier’s measurements can change the billing weight. USFans’ help page describes collecting a shortfall or returning an eligible excess to the account balance; check the parcel details.
faq.sourceTitle: Estimated Billing Weight and Actual Billing Weight — When will the overcharged postage be refunded?

faq.q: Where can I track my USFans parcel?
faq.a: Open the relevant parcel and select Tracking Details. International shipments pass through several stages, so updates may lag behind physical movement. Check the route information and the latest recorded scan when asking support about progress.
faq.sourceTitle: How to check logistics information after the package was sent out?

faq.q: Does a gap in tracking mean the parcel is lost?
faq.a: Not by itself. USFans explains that the first scan and later scans appear at different times for different routes. Compare the gap with your route’s stated expectations and ask support if the shipment needs investigation.
faq.sourceTitle: Why hasn't the tracking been updated since the parcel was shipped?

faq.q: Can I return every item after warehouse QC?
faq.a: No. Eligibility depends on the seller’s return policy, the item category, condition and the time since stock-in. Keep packaging, tags and accessories intact while deciding. Submit a request through the order promptly and confirm any shipping or service charges before proceeding.
faq.sourceTitle: Return and Exchange Rules

faq.q: What should I do if my delivered parcel is damaged or incorrect?
faq.a: Document the packaging and affected items, keep relevant records, and contact USFans promptly through the parcel’s after-sales option. Provide the order, photos and a clear description. Claim periods and outcomes depend on the circumstances and applicable terms, so avoid delaying the report.
faq.sourceTitle: What should I do if there is a problem after I receive the parcel?

articles.title: How to Use a USFans Spreadsheet: Find, Compare and Check a Listing
articles.description: A practical USFans spreadsheet workflow: search with useful terms, compare listing evidence, keep the correct product ID and prepare a clear shortlist.
articles.intro: A USFans spreadsheet is most useful when it helps you make a smaller, better informed shortlist. A long list of links alone does not tell you which size to choose, whether a photo belongs to the current listing, or what shipping will cost. Treat the directory as the beginning of your research. Use it to discover a product, inspect the available evidence and open the matching listing on USFans. This guide explains a repeatable method that works whether you have an exact product name, a broad category or only a rough idea of what you want. The goal is a clear decision, not the largest possible basket.

sections.heading: 1. Decide what a useful result would look like
paragraphs: Before entering a search, write down the product type and the two features that matter most. For a hoodie, those might be the fit and the fastening; for a bag, the opening and the dimensions. A search such as “zip hoodie” gives you a more useful starting point than a collection of unrelated brand names. If you already know an exact model or listing ID, keep that information separate so you can use it to check identity later. Search terms help discovery, while a marketplace and product ID identify a particular listing.

Set an item budget separately from a shipping budget. The visible price is a comparison aid, not a complete delivered total. Also decide whether you need the item soon or are simply exploring. A deadline changes the questions you must ask before purchasing, but it cannot turn an uncertain estimate into a promise. This small amount of preparation makes the next steps quicker: you can remove unsuitable results before spending time studying every photo.

sections.heading: 2. Search broadly, then narrow by one condition
paragraphs: Start with the simplest useful phrase. If the results are too broad, add one distinguishing word or use a relevant category. Avoid changing the category, search phrase and sort order at the same time: when the results change, you will not know which choice helped. A disciplined search usually needs a few deliberate adjustments rather than dozens of random combinations. Keep an eye on the current filter and page so you do not mistake a narrow result set for the complete directory.

Different sorting choices answer different questions. A recent listing is worth inspecting because it is newly visible, not because it has been independently tested. A popular listing may attract attention without matching your requirements. A low price may refer to a different option or a simpler product. Use sorting to arrange candidates for review, then open the details. When you return to the results, preserve your search terms and position so that comparisons remain consistent.

For example, if a broad shoe search gives too many unrelated results, keep the category fixed and try a more descriptive model or use term. If that returns nothing, remove the most specific word before concluding that no suitable listing exists. Search labels are not always written the way a buyer describes a product. This is a discovery technique, not proof that every possible product is present. A no-result search should lead to a revised query or a pause, not an invented product recommendation.

sections.heading: 3. Read a product card as an invitation to inspect
paragraphs: A card normally offers a name, an image and a price reference. That is enough to decide whether to open a record, but not enough to choose a size or judge quality. Short titles may leave out details, and a single image may show one option among many. Read the product page before assuming that a pictured accessory, package or set is included. If the title and image seem inconsistent, treat that as a reason to investigate rather than inventing an explanation.

The most helpful comparison uses the same fields for every candidate. Note the source marketplace, product ID, selected option, listed measurements and unresolved questions. Do not rely on remembering three nearly identical thumbnails. A small note such as “candidate B: zipper, medium, sleeve measurement missing” is more useful than a vague ranking of good and bad. It tells you exactly what information would let you make a decision and what remains uncertain.

sections.heading: 4. Separate seller images from warehouse evidence
paragraphs: Seller images describe or promote a listing. Warehouse QC photographs, when available and correctly associated with an item, show a photographed item at a later stage. These are different kinds of evidence. A large gallery is not automatically a QC gallery, and an attractive studio photo does not confirm what will arrive in your order. Check the image label and the product identity before treating any photograph as proof of a particular size, color or condition.

Historical QC can help you identify questions, such as where a measurement is needed or which detail deserves a closer view. It cannot guarantee that your own item will be identical. If there is no verified QC reference, say so in your shortlist and make the purchase decision with that limitation visible. Do not turn missing evidence into a positive claim. The separate QC guide explains how to review your own warehouse photographs and how to make a precise request when an important detail is not shown.

sections.heading: 5. Open the exact USFans listing
paragraphs: After selecting a candidate, use its purchase link and compare the USFans page with the directory record. Check the marketplace, product ID and product identity before selecting any options. A matching number without a matching marketplace is not a complete match. The same style of numeric ID can appear in different marketplace systems, so copying only the digits can send you to the wrong place.

The product link does not choose a size, color or quantity for you. Read those fields again on USFans, especially when a listing has many thumbnail options. Confirm the current price and any relevant seller notes there. The USFans official beginner guide describes the purchase and later warehouse stages; the directory does not handle your account or payment. If a link loads an unrelated product or a general search page, stop that purchase path and resolve the identity mismatch first.

sections.heading: 6. Build a shortlist that survives the warehouse stage
paragraphs: A useful shortlist is a compact record of your decision. For each item, keep the source marketplace and ID, the desired option, your sizing reference, the price you saw and the date you checked it. Add one sentence explaining why you chose it. That final sentence prevents a common problem: accumulating several similar products and later forgetting what made each one useful. Remove duplicates that do not add a meaningful difference.

Leave space for the next evidence rather than pretending the decision is complete. When your own order reaches the warehouse, compare its photographs and measurements with the record you made before buying. If the wrong option appears, your original notes make the discrepancy easier to describe. If several items are ready for shipping, the same shortlist helps you identify which pieces are approved and which still have an unanswered question. Keep unresolved items out of a parcel decision until you understand the available choices.

sections.heading: 7. Use a stopping rule before adding more products
paragraphs: Search tools make it easy to keep browsing after you already have enough information. Set a stopping rule: compare a manageable number of plausible candidates, choose the one whose evidence best fits your requirements, and record any remaining uncertainty. If none meets the requirements, pause. Buying the least unsuitable result is different from finding a suitable product. The directory should make that distinction clearer, not pressure you into a purchase.

Before leaving the research stage, review the whole shortlist once. Are the source IDs clear? Did you compare measurements instead of size labels alone? Are price references separated from shipping expectations? Is every QC claim backed by an identified photograph? Can you explain why each item is included? Answering these questions gives you a practical handover from discovery to ordering. You can then use the buying, QC and shipping guides at the stage where they are relevant instead of trying to solve every issue at once.

articles.title: How to Buy Weidian Products on USFans: A Careful First Order
articles.description: Follow a Weidian item from its original product ID to the correct USFans listing, option selection, order questions and warehouse review.
keywords: how to buy weidian on usfans
articles.intro: Buying a Weidian item through USFans begins with identifying the right listing. A shared photograph, a seller name and a product number are not interchangeable. The safest practical starting point is a complete original listing or a correctly formed USFans product link, followed by a careful check of the options. This guide focuses on the decisions you control before and after an order. It does not promise a fixed purchase time, a particular payment method for every account, or automatic return eligibility. Those details must be checked in your current USFans order and the applicable official help information.

sections.heading: 1. Keep the original Weidian identity intact
paragraphs: A Weidian link can contain an itemID parameter identifying the seller listing. Keep the complete link until you have confirmed the item on USFans. For the sample used by this directory, the original product number is 7755101935 and the corresponding USFans route uses marketplace channel 3. That is a concrete mapping for this source type, not a reason to treat every long number you see online as a Weidian product ID.

Be careful with identifiers from a directory page. Its own record number may be used to find a local detail page, while the seller listing has a different number. Also distinguish a shop ID, order ID and product ID. They can look similar but serve different purposes. If a friend sends a screenshot without a listing, ask for the original product link. Reconstructing a purchase from an image alone adds uncertainty about the seller and the exact item.

sections.heading: 2. Verify the product after opening USFans
paragraphs: Open the matching product link and inspect the page before proceeding. Check the product type, images, source and available options. A page loading successfully is only a technical result; it does not prove that the item shown is the one you intended. If the page is blank, unavailable or asking for information, do not assume the listing has been confirmed. Keep the original source link available so you can compare or ask a specific question.

Product titles can be abbreviated or translated, so use several details rather than title wording alone. Compare the model, construction, option images and seller references where visible. If one page shows a set and another appears to show a single item, resolve that difference before paying. A helpful order starts with a clearly identified product. It is much harder to explain a mistake later if the only record of your intention is a broad description such as “the black one.”

sections.heading: 3. Choose the option as carefully as the product
paragraphs: A correct listing can still produce an incorrect order if the option selection is careless. Read size, color, package and quantity fields separately. Similar thumbnail images may represent different combinations. A displayed price can change when you select another option, so check the final selection rather than relying on the first amount you saw. Record the option name exactly as shown if it is easy to confuse with another choice.

For clothing, compare the seller's measurements with a garment you already own and like. Decide whether the measurements describe the garment or a body size, and make sure the units match. For accessories, inspect dimensions and closure details instead of assuming that a familiar photograph means a familiar size. Where information is missing, make a focused enquiry. One clear question about a sleeve length or included component is easier to answer than asking whether the item is “good.”

sections.heading: 4. Review the order before submitting payment
paragraphs: Use the review step to check product identity, selected options, quantity and destination information together. Read the current amounts displayed in the account and distinguish the item purchase from later international shipping. The official USFans guide places item and local delivery payment before the warehouse and international parcel stages. Do not treat a low item price as a quote for the complete journey to your address.

Write remarks only where they add useful information. A remark can clarify an exact requirement, but it should not replace selecting the correct visible option. Avoid conflicting instructions such as selecting one size while asking for another in a note. If a requirement is essential, confirm that it can be fulfilled before ordering. Keep your own record of the final choice and review screen. That record helps you compare the result later without relying on memory.

sections.heading: 5. Respond to purchase questions with specific information
paragraphs: After submission, monitor the order for messages that require a response. The official guide describes an order enquiry route for communication during purchasing. A question about stock, price or an incomplete option needs a deliberate choice from you. Reading an update is different from resolving it. Before replying, check which item and which option the message concerns, particularly if you have several similar orders.

A useful reply states the desired outcome and any acceptable alternative. For example, you can say that a different color is acceptable only if the size remains the same, or that you prefer not to substitute at all. Avoid a vague approval if the proposed change affects the reason you chose the product. When a seller cannot supply the selected option, return to your requirements rather than making a rushed replacement. The fact that another option is available does not make it equivalent.

sections.heading: 6. Check your own warehouse item
paragraphs: When warehouse information becomes available, compare it with the order you actually placed. Start with identity and quantity, then inspect the selected option and visible condition. Keep source images and your own warehouse photographs in separate roles: one shows the listing presentation, the other helps assess the received item. The inspection process is useful, but photographs cannot answer every question about fit, material performance or long-term durability.

If something important is unclear, describe the missing evidence. Ask for the measurement or view that would change your decision, using the current service options and charges shown in your account. If there is a mismatch, keep it tied to the specific order and selected option. Do not approve a parcel simply because other items are ready. Consult the relevant official help information for the available return or exchange process and act on the actual order status rather than assuming an outcome.

The official inspection-scope entry makes an important distinction for clothing: the warehouse check considers the selected information and the garment's label, while actual fit and size differences are outside that basic inspection scope. A label showing your chosen size therefore does not answer whether the garment will fit as expected. If measurements are central to your decision, arrange the appropriate additional evidence through the current service options. For electronics, the same help entry describes an appearance check rather than a power-on test. Choose products with those limits in mind.

sections.heading: 7. Move to shipping only after the item decision is clear
paragraphs: The warehouse stage and the international shipping stage solve different problems. First decide which items are ready to send. Then evaluate the eligible shipping options for the group you want to ship, including packing needs and any restrictions shown by the service. Combining more items may change dimensions and route eligibility. It should be a considered parcel decision, not an automatic next click because you have finished shopping.

For a first order, keeping the item selection manageable makes it easier to understand where each piece of information comes from. Record the order number, approved option, warehouse decision and parcel association. When the parcel is dispatched, use the tracking information associated with that parcel rather than an older seller-to-warehouse tracking number. At delivery, compare what you receive with your records. This closes the loop from source listing to received item and gives your next purchase a clearer reference point.

articles.title: USFans QC Photos: Checklist & Measurement Requests
articles.description: Check USFans warehouse QC photos for the right item, size and visible defects. Use clear requests for missing details before shipping.
articles.intro: QC photographs are useful when you connect them to a specific question. They can help you notice the wrong option, an obvious visible problem or a measurement that deserves attention. They do not turn a product into a guaranteed purchase, and they cannot establish every claim about its materials or performance. The first task is to identify which item the pictures represent. The second is to decide whether the available views answer the questions that matter to you. This checklist is designed for a calm, evidence-led review before you include an item in an international parcel.

sections.heading: 1. Identify the image type and the item
paragraphs: Begin by asking where the image came from. A seller gallery, a historical QC reference and photographs of your own warehouse order should not be treated as the same thing. Seller pictures can help explain the intended design. A historical reference may show one previously photographed item. Your own order photographs are the relevant starting point for checking the item associated with your purchase. Keep those distinctions visible when saving or comparing images.

Match the record to the marketplace, product ID, selected option and quantity. A similar-looking product from the same seller is not enough. Check whether the photos show the color and size you selected, rather than assuming a matching thumbnail proves the whole order. If a gallery has no clear association with a listing, use it as inspiration at most. A credible QC review begins with an identity match, not with confidence inspired by an attractive picture.

rows: Item and option
Order reference, color and size label
Compare your received item with your actual order
Visible condition
Overall view and close-up of the concern
Describe the exact mark, seam or mismatch
Sizing uncertainty
Flat garment or relevant shoe measurement
Confirm service availability and cost before requesting
Missing information
Which decision the extra view would answer
Keep the item out of an international parcel until resolved

sections.heading: 2. Review the whole item before small details
paragraphs: Start with the broad shape and completeness. Look at front and back views where available, then compare the silhouette with the selected option. Check whether a pair or set appears complete and whether any included components that matter to you are visible. This broad review can reveal a wrong version or missing piece before you spend time inspecting a small seam or print. Keep your initial findings descriptive: what is visible, what differs and what is not shown.

Do not judge proportion from one angle alone. A garment folded on a table can look wider or shorter than it is. A bag photographed close to a camera can have a distorted shape. Compare multiple views before deciding that something is misaligned. If you still see a concern, name its location and explain the comparison you are making. A specific observation is easier to verify than a general statement that the product “looks strange.”

sections.heading: 3. Compare dimensions using a consistent method
paragraphs: Measurements become useful only when the method is clear. A flat chest width is not the same as a circumference. A sleeve measured from one starting point may not match a seller chart measured from another. Before comparing numbers, check the units, measurement points and whether the item is laid flat without stretching. Use a garment or accessory you already own as a practical reference when possible, measured in the same way.

Choose the dimensions that affect your use. For a jacket, those might be chest width, body length and sleeve length. For a bag, the opening and internal space may matter more than the external height. Requesting every possible number creates work without necessarily improving the decision. Instead, identify which uncertain dimension would make you accept or reject the item. Explain that measurement clearly when using any available photo or measurement service, and check the current service conditions first.

sections.heading: 4. Describe visible concerns without overclaiming
paragraphs: A photo may show a mark, a loose thread, an uneven edge or a difference in placement. Describe the visible evidence without claiming to know its cause. A pale patch could be lighting or a surface issue; a curved edge might reflect how the item was placed. Zooming can help locate a concern, but excessive enlargement can turn image compression into apparent damage. Return to the full image and another angle before drawing a conclusion.

Use neutral wording when asking for clarification. State the area, the visible issue and the additional view that would help. For example, ask whether a mark remains in a closer photograph under ordinary lighting. If a functional issue matters, photographs alone may not settle it. Do not infer durability, waterproofing, battery safety or authenticity from visual resemblance. The practical result of a QC review should be a supported decision or a focused question, not a list of impressive-sounding certifications.

sections.heading: 5. Make additional photo requests actionable
paragraphs: A good request tells the person taking the photo exactly what to show. Identify the item, the side or component, the angle and any measurement points. Keep one requirement per request where that improves clarity. If you need to compare the left and right side, say that both should appear under similar conditions. If a closure is the concern, ask for the view that shows it, rather than requesting several unrelated close-ups.

Check which services are currently available for the order and whether a charge or limitation applies. Do not assume every request is included or that every product can be tested. Prioritize evidence that would change your decision. A second photograph of an already clear detail adds little value, while a missing dimension can be decisive. When the new evidence arrives, compare it with the original concern and close that question explicitly before creating another request.

USFans describes standard photographs as fixed-angle images and Detailed Photo as a separate service for a chosen view or measurement. That distinction suggests a useful request format: identify the warehouse item, name the detail and explain how it should be shown. For a width measurement, specify the two points rather than asking for a general size check. A request to photograph a label is different from a request to measure the garment. Read the current Detailed Photo help entry and the order screen for the available conditions before purchasing an additional service.

sections.heading: 6. Separate approval, clarification and after-sales decisions
paragraphs: Give each item a clear next action. One item may be ready for shipping, another may need a measurement, and a third may need an order enquiry about an incorrect option. Keeping those states separate avoids treating the whole haul as approved because most of it looks acceptable. Record the issue and the date you raised it. If several orders look alike, include the order reference so that messages do not become detached from the item.

Return and exchange choices depend on the seller, product and current order circumstances. Read the relevant official help and the response tied to your order instead of assuming a universal right or a guaranteed result. Preserve the original selection and the evidence of the mismatch when you explain the problem. Do not keep an item waiting indefinitely without checking its current storage and service conditions. A clear record helps you make the next decision while the relevant options can still be assessed.

sections.heading: 7. Finish with a short record for parcel planning
paragraphs: Once the review is complete, write a brief final note: item identity checked, important dimensions reviewed, visible concerns resolved or consciously accepted, and remaining limits understood. Keep the approved option associated with the item. That note is especially helpful when you have several similar pieces and return to the warehouse later. It prevents a previously unresolved item from being included in a parcel by accident.

QC approval is one input to shipping, not a shipping quote. Packing choices, eligible routes and final parcel measurements are separate considerations. A bulky or fragile item may need a different packing decision even when its visible condition is acceptable. The official USFans beginner guide places warehouse review before selecting stored items for delivery; use that sequence to keep the decisions clear. Review the selected parcel contents once more and make sure every included item has a deliberate, documented outcome.

articles.title: USFans Shipping Cost: Compare Weight, Parcel Size and Packing Choices
articles.description: Understand the inputs behind a USFans shipping estimate and compare eligible routes using the same parcel assumptions, without relying on a fixed price per kilogram.
articles.intro: A useful USFans shipping estimate starts with a well-defined parcel. The number of products in a basket is not enough: item weight, packed dimensions, destination, contents and selected services can all change the comparison. A rate quoted for someone else's parcel may be a poor guide to yours. This article explains how to organize the information you need, compare eligible options on consistent assumptions and understand why an early estimate can differ from the final charge. It does not provide a live quote or a universal shipping rate. Use the amounts and conditions shown for your own parcel on USFans.

sections.heading: 1. Separate item spending from parcel spending
paragraphs: Build two lists before comparing shipping. The first covers the products you plan to buy, their selected options and the purchase amounts shown at that stage. The second covers the international parcel and the services associated with sending it. Keeping them separate makes it easier to understand which choice changed the total. Adding a product can affect both lists, while choosing a different packing option may primarily affect the parcel calculation.

Do not divide an incomplete total by the number of items and call that a delivered cost. You may not yet know the packed size or the route available for the contents. Instead, record what is known and label what remains estimated. This is a simple budgeting method, not a promise that every cost can be predicted in advance. If an item is only attractive at the lowest imaginable shipping amount, consider whether the purchase still makes sense under a less favorable estimate.

sections.heading: 2. Start from the actual group you want to send
paragraphs: Make a parcel candidate list using items that are ready for a shipping decision. Include the quantity and any packing characteristics that matter, such as a rigid shape, a large retail box or a part that needs protection. A hypothetical future purchase should not quietly change the assumptions of a quote you are comparing today. If you want to consider adding it, create a second scenario and label the difference.

Check the delivery destination and the contents information carefully. Eligible services can depend on those inputs. Do not assume that a route visible for clothing will also be available after adding a different product type. If the platform asks for more information, provide an accurate description rather than selecting a convenient category merely to make a route appear. For product-specific restrictions, use the current official information or order support before committing to the purchase or parcel.

sections.heading: 3. Understand why weight alone is incomplete
paragraphs: The official USFans beginner guide explains that the early shipping deposit uses estimated item weight, destination and shipment method, while the final calculation considers the parcel size and weight verified for shipping. The practical implication is that a single weight figure cannot explain every change in a quote. A parcel's external dimensions and the selected service conditions also matter. Read the current method used by the route rather than importing a formula from another service.

When comparing two packing scenarios, write down both weight and dimensions if available. A lighter parcel is not automatically the cheaper one under every route's billing rules. A product that takes up considerable space may alter the comparison differently from a compact item of similar weight. Avoid publishing or relying on a universal divisor unless the specific route states it. The useful question is which verified parcel inputs the selected service uses and whether your estimate reflects them accurately.

The dedicated official weight help distinguishes an estimated billing weight from the actual billing weight determined after packing and logistics measurement. It also explains why removing packaging can change the result. Keep these labels attached to the values you record: an item weight, an estimated parcel billing weight and a final parcel billing weight are not three interchangeable numbers. If one figure changes, identify the stage it belongs to before comparing it with another. This prevents a false discrepancy caused simply by comparing a product measurement with a packed-shipment measurement.

sections.heading: 4. Treat packing as a protection decision as well as a price decision
paragraphs: Retail packaging can add space, but removing it is not always appropriate. Think about the product's shape, surface and vulnerability before choosing a packing change. A structured accessory may need support; a delicate component may need separation from heavier items. The lowest estimated shipping amount is not a complete comparison if achieving it removes protection you consider necessary. Describe the packing outcome you want in clear, practical terms.

The official guide lists optional packing-related services, but availability and conditions should be checked for the current parcel. Compare only the choices you can actually select. Keep a note of what is being removed, retained or reinforced so that the final result can be understood later. Do not assume that a service name tells you every detail of how an item will be packed. Ask for clarification when a specific protection requirement is central to your decision.

sections.heading: 5. Compare routes with the same assumptions
paragraphs: A fair route comparison uses the same destination, parcel contents, dimensions, weight and service selections. If one estimate includes a packing service and another does not, the totals are not directly comparable. Record the date and the inputs alongside each amount, then read the stated conditions. An estimate without its assumptions quickly becomes misleading when the contents or packing plan changes.

Look beyond the displayed total. Consider the route's current eligibility, stated delivery estimate, tracking information and service conditions. A delivery estimate is not a guaranteed arrival date. If you have an important deadline, allow for the stages before international dispatch as well as the international journey itself. Avoid treating the quickest number on a comparison screen as a promise. When a condition is unclear, resolve it before selecting the route rather than discovering the meaning after the parcel is already moving.

sections.heading: 6. Compare consolidation and splitting as separate scenarios
paragraphs: Putting several items in one parcel can change the relationship between packing and shipping charges, but it is not a universal rule that a larger parcel is always better. A mixed group may need more protective packing or different eligible routes. Splitting creates separate parcels with their own conditions. To make a useful comparison, write down the actual contents of each scenario and calculate them using the current options shown by the platform.

Do not compare a combined parcel at one weight assumption with split parcels at another. Keep the inputs consistent and record any uncertainty. Also consider your tolerance for waiting: holding ready items while another purchase arrives is a timing choice as well as a parcel choice. Check the current storage conditions for the items involved. The purpose of comparing scenarios is to understand the tradeoffs clearly, not to prove that one packing strategy always saves money.

sections.heading: 7. Reconcile the estimate with the final parcel record
paragraphs: When the final parcel information becomes available, compare it with the inputs you used earlier. Look for changes in weight, dimensions, contents or selected services before assuming the difference is an error. Keep the earlier estimate and the final record together so that you can ask a precise question if something remains unexplained. A message identifying one changed measurement is easier to investigate than a general complaint that shipping became expensive.

For the next order, use this record as a personal reference for similar goods, while keeping its date and route context visible. It is still an example, not a fixed tariff. Seller packaging, available services and shipping conditions can change. The most useful result of the exercise is a better method: define the parcel, compare consistent inputs, read the current terms and review the final figures. That method remains useful even when the displayed rates no longer match your previous shipment.

articles.title: USFans Product Links Explained: Marketplace Codes, IDs and Common Errors
articles.description: Understand USFans product URLs, the difference between directory and marketplace IDs, and a practical checklist for checking a link before selecting options.
articles.intro: A product link carries several pieces of information that should stay together. The marketplace identifies the source system; the product ID identifies a listing within that system; other parameters may record a referral or page state. Copying only the digits or replacing a marketplace code without checking the source can create a plausible-looking but incorrect URL. This guide explains the current USFans product route and a practical way to validate it. It also explains what a correct link cannot do: it does not confirm stock, choose the right option, prove product quality or guarantee that a listing will remain available.

sections.heading: 1. Read the hostname, route and parameters separately
paragraphs: Start with the hostname so you know which service will receive the visit. For the purchase links used here, the destination is www.usfans.com. The product route then contains a marketplace channel and a product ID. In the example https://www.usfans.com/product/3/7755101935?ref=SWD92F, the route identifies channel 3 and listing 7755101935. The ref value is a separate parameter. It is not part of the product number and should not be pasted into a product ID field.

This separation is useful when a shared link looks complicated. First identify the destination, then identify the listing, then inspect the remaining parameters. Do not assume that every query parameter is unnecessary, and do not add parameters whose meaning you have not verified. When sharing a link, keep the correct source identity intact. A shorter link is not an improvement if shortening it removes information needed to open the intended product.

sections.heading: 2. Use the marketplace channel that matches the original source
paragraphs: The USFans official application checked for this guide defines channel 1 as 1688, channel 2 as Taobao and channel 3 as Weidian. These codes explain why a product URL needs more than a numeric ID. A Weidian product should not be opened under the Taobao channel simply because the number is accepted as text in the address bar. Matching the marketplace is part of identifying the listing.

Treat the mapping as a verified current implementation detail, not an excuse to guess how every other source is handled. If a listing comes from a marketplace or link form you have not checked, use the official workflow and verify the resulting product page. A future platform change can also affect a route. The final practical test is whether the destination shows the intended source listing and its current options. A mechanically valid URL is only the beginning of that check.

sections.heading: 3. Distinguish directory records from seller product IDs
paragraphs: A recommendation directory may assign its own record number to organize pages. That number can differ completely from the original marketplace product ID. In the sample record used for this project, directory record 6681 refers to Weidian product 7755101935. The purchase route must use the marketplace product number. Substituting the directory record number would change the target rather than preserve the listing.

The same caution applies to shop numbers, order references and parcel references. Each belongs to a different context. When copying an identifier, record what it identifies, not just its digits. A useful note is “Weidian product ID,” followed by the number and the source link. If you cannot tell which kind of ID you have, return to the original page before building a purchase link. This avoids errors that can be hard to notice when all the fields look numeric.

sections.heading: 4. Preserve the selected product, then recheck its options
paragraphs: A correct product route usually identifies the listing, while the buyer still needs to inspect and choose the relevant options. Do not assume that a link shared beside a picture selects the pictured color or size. A seller can offer several models, quantities or packages inside one listing. The first visible image and price may not describe the option you want. Recheck the selection on the destination page before proceeding.

If you are sharing a recommendation with someone else, describe the intended option separately and avoid saying that the link guarantees it. Include the option wording and the feature that distinguishes it, such as a fastening or package count. The recipient should still compare it with the current page. This approach is more reliable than relying on a thumbnail that may change or on an abbreviated title that leaves out important differences between options.

sections.heading: 5. Diagnose a link problem in a useful order
paragraphs: When a link fails, first record what actually happened. Did the browser show an error, did the application load without a product, or did it display a different item? Those are different problems. Confirm the hostname and inspect whether punctuation was accidentally added during copying. A trailing period from a sentence or an incomplete copied query can change how a link is interpreted. Keep the original message available while checking it.

Next compare the marketplace and product ID with the original source. If those match but the listing is unavailable, do not invent a replacement ID. The seller may have changed or removed the listing, or the application may need another step. Check the current official page and use a precise enquiry if necessary. If the product is different, stop before selecting options. Repeatedly changing numeric codes until something loads can produce a convincing but unrelated product page.

Keep a failed-link note short enough to be useful: the complete original address, the destination you opened, the observed result and the time of the check. Avoid replacing the original with your edited version before recording it, because that removes the evidence needed to understand the error. If a copied link came from a social post, check whether the visible text and the actual destination were different. You do not need to understand every part of a website's software to do this; you only need to preserve the source and describe the result accurately.

sections.heading: 6. Understand what referral parameters do not establish
paragraphs: The purchase links configured for this directory preserve the supplied ref=SWD92F parameter. Its presence is visible in the URL. That fact alone does not establish a discount, a particular coupon, a changed product price or successful account attribution. Do not infer those outcomes merely from a referral-looking parameter. Check the current information shown by USFans if a promotion or account benefit matters to your decision.

Registration is a separate route. The supplied registration address for this project is https://www.usfans.com/register, without an added referral parameter. Keeping that address as supplied avoids silently changing the user's chosen destination. More generally, a product referral parameter and a registration process should not be treated as interchangeable. A clear directory states where a button goes and lets the official service display the current account and purchase terms.

sections.heading: 7. Keep a compact link validation record
paragraphs: For a product you plan to buy, record the original marketplace, original product ID, current USFans URL and the date you checked it. Add the intended option and any unresolved mismatch. This is enough to preserve the important relationship without copying a whole page of unrelated information. If the source listing later changes, you will at least know which record you originally evaluated and what you intended to choose.

Use the same checklist whenever you open a new purchase link: correct destination, correct marketplace, correct product number, matching product identity and freshly checked options. Then move to the separate price, sizing and QC decisions. A well-formed link solves the identity problem; it does not solve every purchasing problem. Keeping those stages distinct makes the process easier to review and helps you explain a specific issue if you need assistance before completing an order.
